# Scormly

> Scormly is a free, open-source (MIT), local-first course builder that runs entirely in the
> browser and exports SCORM 1.2, SCORM 2004 and cmi5 (xAPI) packages for Moodle, TalentLMS,
> SCORM Cloud and virtually any standards-compliant LMS. There is no backend and no account:
> courses, media and comments stay on the author's device, and packages are built client-side.

Scormly is a block-based authoring tool: an author builds a course out of lessons, and each
lesson out of blocks, editing them in place (WYSIWYG) with drag-and-drop and undo/redo. The
interface is in English, Ukrainian, French, Spanish and German. It works in current desktop browsers; Chrome and Edge
can also save a project straight to a folder on disk.

## Where a project lives

- **In the browser** (Chrome, Edge, Firefox): kept in the browser's private storage (OPFS),
  saved automatically, still there after a reload. One click to start.
- **In a folder on disk** (Chrome, Edge — File System Access API): `project.json`, an
  `assets/` folder with the media, `AGENTS.md`, `user-instructions.md` and, once there are
  review comments, `comments.json`. Saved automatically; easy to back up, sync or put in Git.
- **As a project .zip**: the same files in one archive. Any project downloads as a .zip and
  any browser opens one — for backups, sharing with colleagues or handing to an AI assistant.
  A .zip of a project that is already open can update it (one undoable step) or open as new.

## Blocks

- **Text:** heading, paragraph (rich text with links, lists, tables and inline images), list,
  quote, note / callout, columns, table, code.
- **Media:** image, gallery / carousel, image & text, video (captions, transcript, optional
  "must watch to continue"), audio, embed, attachment (downloadable file).
- **Widget:** custom HTML / CSS / JavaScript, or an uploaded .html page or .zip site, for
  simulations, calculators and mini-games. It gets the course theme and a small CSS kit, and
  has "Copy instructions for AI" so a chat assistant can write the page.
- **Explainers:** process diagram, step-by-step guide, timeline, comparison, before / after
  slider, tabs, accordion, flashcards, image hotspots.
- **Practice and assessment:** quiz (single choice, multiple choice, matching, ordering and
  fill-in-the-blanks questions mixed under one Submit, with feedback and a passing score),
  sort-the-order and fill-in-the-blanks exercises, branching dialogue scenario (classic or
  chat / messenger layout), reflection.
- **Navigation:** Continue (reveals the rest of a lesson, optionally only after the tasks
  above it are done), divider, course outline.
- Ready-made block templates and per-block styles (theme or photo backgrounds, spacing,
  full-width bands).

## Course design and export

- A cover page before the first lesson; 10 themes (Rose, Ocean, Forest, Sunset, Mono, Indigo,
  Crimson, Mint, Grape, Terminal) plus a custom accent color and corner shape; every theme
  keeps WCAG AA contrast.
- Course settings: completion rule, pass / fail scoring, free or linear navigation, lesson
  progress, a custom finish message, and the language of the player's buttons and messages
  (English, Ukrainian, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Dutch, Portuguese, or automatic).
- Accessible output aimed at WCAG 2.1 AA: keyboard and screen-reader support, captions and
  transcripts, a learner accessibility menu (text size, high contrast, readable spacing,
  reduced motion).
- A pre-export check flags empty lessons, missing media, questions without a correct answer
  and accessibility gaps such as missing alt text or captions.
- Exports: SCORM 1.2, SCORM 2004 (4th edition) and cmi5, with resume, time spent, score,
  pass / fail, per-quiz objectives and detailed question interactions reported to the LMS.
  Packages include the official schema files; SCORM output is tested on SCORM Cloud.
- In-app preview of the learner view, guided tour, Q&A, release notes and keyboard
  shortcuts (press `?`). Installable as a web app (PWA).

## Review comments

Authors and reviewers comment on any block, reply and resolve, with no accounts — a reviewer
just types a name. Comments live in the project's `comments.json` (never in the course or an
export) and travel in the project .zip; when a reviewer's .zip comes back, their comments
merge into the author's.

## For AI assistants

- Every project (folder or .zip) contains `AGENTS.md`, generated by Scormly: it documents
  `project.json` — the whole course as one JSON file — every block type's `data` shape, the
  Widget page spec and `comments.json`. An assistant can read it and then edit or write a
  whole course, or work through the open review comments and reply to each one.
- `user-instructions.md` holds the author's own notes for AI (tone, audience, conventions);
  it is edited in Project settings → AI assistant and never overwritten by Scormly.
- Scormly repairs a hand- or AI-edited `project.json` when it is opened (ids, types, missing
  fields) and reports what it fixed.
- To hand a project to an assistant: download it as a .zip (or point the assistant at the
  project folder), ask it to follow `AGENTS.md`, then open the .zip it returns.
